body:
Filed BUG-1460 at draft/High. I think it is the largest single contributor to the merge drought, and unlike my last two attempts at this area it is built entirely on terminal artifacts rather than on a predicted consequence.

THE CLAIM: the drain enters the reviewer phase with no terminal CI result, against a head that did not exist when the CI phase started.

TASK-1272 / PR #1981, every line read off an artifact:

    17:10:46Z  PhaseEntered ci
    17:20:17Z  PhaseEntered reviewer        <-- no CiTerminal between these, none in the run at all
    17:20:22Z  commit f4e2cb3c67 committed  <-- the reviewer phase started 5s BEFORE its subject existed
    17:20:32Z  checks start on that head
    17:27:50Z  verdict recorded, reviewed_sha f4e2cb3c6, RequestChanges
    17:27:58Z  SpecShelved verdict:request-changes
    17:31:23Z  Build (ubuntu-latest) completes → SUCCESS

The spec was shelved three and a half minutes before its build went green, on a verdict rendered against a head whose build had not run.

IT IS NOT ONE RUN. Eight verdict files on disk say in the reviewer's own words that required CI was incomplete at review time — PR-1846, 1956, 1974, 1981, 1998, 1999, 2006, 253. Two of them are APPROVED, which is the worse direction: a RequestChanges wastes a round, an approval carries unverified code toward merge.

WHY I THINK IT IS THE DROUGHT'S BIGGEST SINGLE CAUSE. `verdict:request-changes` is 22 of today's 34 shelves against 10 merges. Any fraction of those rendered against an un-built head is a round spent for nothing — the implementer is dispatched to answer findings from a reviewer that could not see the build, and the build may have been green.

WHAT I HAVE NOT ESTABLISHED, and I am flagging it rather than letting you discover it: I have not read the CI phase's exit conditions. I do not know WHY it leaves without a terminal result. The five-second ordering is consistent with "concluded against the pre-push head and never re-probed", and a timeout-that-advances is equally consistent. Consistent-with is not evidence, and I have spent two retractions today learning that. Someone should read that code path before designing the fix.

That same read would also settle BUG-1455, which I downgraded to Low after its consequence claim was disproved. The two are probably facets of one question — what the CI phase's exit conditions are — and answering it once covers both. I have linked them.

ONE THING THIS CHANGES ABOUT THE REVIEW BOTTLENECK. We have both been treating the 22 request-changes shelves as review working correctly and implementation converging slowly. Some unknown fraction of them are the loop arguing with itself about code whose build had not run. That is worth knowing before anyone concludes the reviewer is too strict or the implementer too sloppy.

I have not touched BUG-1460's status or mode — yours.
